title: EU residency compliance: auditable routing decisions + soft-fallback strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide an auditable, customer-scoped routing enforcement layer that guarantees EU-only handling for opt-in accounts while offering an approved 'soft-fallback' path when capacity or model compatibility requires a non-EU runtime. The feature must: 1) evaluate per-request residency constraints (tenant-level flags, consent headers, contract clauses), 2) enforce region selection and tier routing with deterministic decision outputs, 3) emit a tamper-evident audit record for every decision (PDS input, matched rule, routed endpoint, fallback reason), and 4) support customer allowlist/denylist overrides and emergency escape hatches.

We must avoid hard-blocking production traffic in non-emergency flows: soft-fallback should attempt an allowed EU-compatible model variant first, and only when that is unavailable fall back to a non-EU variant after applying automatic data-mitigation transformations and logging customer consent/exception metadata. Data-mitigation transforms are a runtime step (prefix-redaction, ephemeral KV masking) applied only for fallback flows and reversible only by authorized SRE/legal workflows.

This ticket covers the policy schema, router integration, audit schema, and operational runbook for canary and incident handling. Implementation will include API/console controls for tenant allowlist/denylist management (read-only for most roles), runtime flags, telemetry hooks, and retention policy for audit records (KMS-backed storage, retention configurable per customer SLA).
acceptance_criteria: Every routed request for tenants with eu_residency=required emits an audit record with fields: request_id, tenant_id, policy_version, matched_rule_id, decision, target_region, target_model, fallback_reason (if any), timestamp, operator_id (if manual override)
Policy engine supports tenant-level allowlist/denylist and a precedence order: denylist > tenant flag > global policy > emergency override

Soft-fallback path attempts EU-compatible variant first; if unavailable after configurable timeout (default 250ms), route to non-EU variant only after applying configured mitigation transforms and recording explicit fallback metadata
Admin console shows per-tenant routing status and the last 10 audit decisions; RBAC limits who can view/modify allowlists
End-to-end tests that simulate EU capacity loss trigger the fallback path and produce audit events which appear in the monitoring dashboard within 60s

SLOs: routing decision latency p50 + policy evaluation overhead < 5ms, p95 < 20ms (measured in nightlies), and fallback telemetry does not increase overall 95th percentile tail beyond 10% for affected routes
technical_design: Policy Decision Service (PDS) extension: add "residency_rules" to policy schema. New rule attributes: region_constraints, allowed_model_variants, mitigation_transforms, precedence, expiry. Policies are versioned and signed with a PKI keypair for tamper-evidence.

Router integration: router consults PDS synchronously with request metadata (tenant_id, route, model_hint, consent_headers). PDS returns decision object including primary_target and fallback_candidates. Router applies decision deterministically; logs decision to audit stream as a single envelope event.

Fallback adapter: library that orchestrates EU-first attempt -> timeout -> mitigation -> non-EU route. Exposes hooks for token-prefix scrub, KV-mask, and ephemeral context flags. Must be pluggable per runtime (hosted, dedicated, private).

Audit log format: newline-delimited JSON events with immutable fields. Events written to an append-only KMS-backed bucket and to internal Kafka topic for low-latency observability. Example fields listed in acceptance criteria. Retention: default 90 days; enterprise tenants can request 7 years via Private plan.

Operational controls: feature flag for 'soft-fallback-enabled' per-region and per-tenant; console UI to add/remove tenants from allowlist/denylist; emergency circuit-breaker to revert to hard-deny for specific tenants.

Security and privacy: mitigation_transforms implemented as pipeline stages that do not store redacted tokens in persistent logs; KMS encrypts audit records; access to raw audit records gated by RBAC and audit trail.

Backward compatibility: policy_version field ensures old routers gracefully handle a missing field by defaulting to current global policy. Migration plan included for existing residency gates (see dependencies).
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (FF off) - internal QA: merge PDS schema and router integration behind feature flag, run unit and integration tests
Stage 1 (Canary 5%) - enable for small set of synthetic tenants and internal customers; monitor for routing errors and latency regressions for 72 hours
Stage 2 (Gradual 25/50/100) - incrementally enable by customer cohort and region; validate audit completeness and retention behavior
Stage 3 - enable console controls and open self-serve allowlist for targeted beta customers; collect feedback and compliance signoff
Emergency plan - circuit breaker: immediate FF flip to hard-deny for tenant or global if audit shows sensitive leakage or legal objection; runbook with SRE and Legal contacts included in links
test_plan: Unit tests: policy schema validation, precedence logic, mitigation_transform application. 100% coverage on decision paths
Integration tests: router + PDS + fallback adapter end-to-end in staging. Inject latency and model-unavailability to force fallback paths
Contract tests: ensure audit event schema compatibility between writer and downstream consumers (dashboards, billing pipeline)
Performance tests: nightlies that measure p50/p95 policy eval overhead across route types under realistic token distributions
Chaos tests: simulate EU region outage and verify canary customers hit fallback and that mitigation transforms are applied correctly
Security tests: verify audit records are encrypted at rest, RBAC applied, and mitigation transforms do not leak raw tokens into logs
open_questions: What is the max acceptable mitigation transform latency budget before fallback is considered failed? Proposal: 100ms added to the per-request budget
Legal needs to approve the exact fields that constitute an acceptable 'audit record' for EU tenants. Contact: legal@redwood.com — awaiting signoff
How should Private deployments expose allowlist UI? Proposal: config-only for on-prem with a CLI helper; console UI remains for hosted/dedicated
Retention SLAs for enterprise customers requiring >2 years; need input from Sales on packaging and pricing
